page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-320s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical AMD EPYC core (2 threads per core) operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 16.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally bundled with a 320 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance contrasted by aggregate multi-core limits. In stress-ng, single-core CPU throughput reached 3,423.78 (top tier), accompanied by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,100.0 (top 25%) and rapid single-threaded compression speeds of 32.1 GB/sec for gzip and 14.63 GB/sec for bzip3. However, overall multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit, as seen in the PassMark CPU score of 5,977.93 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3,757.0 (both in the bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth performs within average thresholds for uncached 256 MB operations (76.83 GB/sec read, 73.9 GB/sec write), but cached 16 KB read throughput placed in the lower quartile at 322.23 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this instance lies between its substantial memory and storage allocation versus limited parallel execution capacity. With 16 GB of RAM and 320 GB of fast NVMe storage attached to just 2 dedicated vCPUs, it delivers solid resource density for memory-dependent tasks without the expense of higher core counts. Conversely, high-concurrency tasks encounter performance bottlenecks, as evidenced by modest Redis SET throughput (5.47 million ops/sec) and low static web serving bandwidth (2.28 GB/sec).

This server profile fits lightweight memory-bound workloads, single-threaded processing pipelines, text processing, intermediate caching tiers, and localized staging environments where fast local disk storage and generous memory per core outweigh the need for parallel compute throughput.
